Summary: [ASUS][B3B5P5][PTL] Under UEFI, WiFi disconnection during downloading recovery image
Custom field (Root Cause):
1 driver issue fixed and 1 BIOS TCP level configuration change:

1. driver fix:
IWL_TX_DMA_MASK was set to 0xFFFFFFFFF (36-bit), a leftover from gen1
code. GEN2 and future devices support full 64-bit DMA addressing and

silently dropping TFD entries while advancing the TXQ write pointer.
This leads to firmware assertions and TXQ watchdog timeouts.
The fix removes the obsolete 36‑bit DMA mask and the associated validation check, allowing proper handling of 64‑bit DMA addresses.

Summary: [HP][IEC][Merino][Win11 25H2][PTL][WhP2/GfP2][SIO2455614] Device sometimes cannot connect to WPA3-Enterprise EAP-TLS Unifi AP
Custom field (Root Cause):
AP behavior:
After STA G3, the AP retains the old session state and has an SA Query in progress. As a result, it correctly rejects the STA Association Request with status 30 (comeback). The STA waits for the comeback interval and then retries the association. At this point, since the interval has elapsed, the AP should accept the request. Instead, the AP sends a Deauthentication frame with reason code 6 (CLASS2_FRAME_FROM_NONAUTH_STA), which is non-compliant behavior.

Why the reconnect fails:
The driver correctly treats reason code 6 as recoverable and initiates a fresh connection attempt. However, a race condition in the driver can cause this retry to fail, leading to “No suitable network found” / “No enabled networks,” and don't try to do actual connection.
In addition, when we retrigger a connection, we are not preserving the connect token, so even if we'll be able to connect the driver will eventually fail. Fix both issues.

Summary: [MSFT][UID 1252477][PTL][FmP] SoC stuck in C2 state after changing Wi-Fi SAR indexes with TAS enabled on Windows 11 25H2

But when TAS is enabled, GMPD doesn't care about SAR limit since TAS can decide to ignore SAR limit, so GMPD must calibrate without SAR consideration. So when SAR has changed, GMPD requested paging. WiFi FW runs FSEQ. As part of FSEQ it sets FINE locks (in particular AUX_HW_LOCK_2)
There is a logic in the top that prevent HW to write to registers when AUX_HW_LOCK_2 is set and relevant func_state is LOW
Relevant logic preventing BT OTP Reader (usee BT UMAC master) writing to Aux while BT func_state is LOW:
bt_umac_aux_connect_we_func_lock    = (~scu_aux_hw_lock_2 || bt_scu_func_state) && bt_umac_aux_connect_we;
When BIOS switches BT I/F to IOSF, BT HW kicks BT OTP Reader
OTP Reader tries writing to Aux register to enable OTP, but fails due to the early lock (BT func_state is LOW on this HW stage)
All next reads from OTP are failed since OTP is not enabled
BT config space remains with default values. In specific Sub_System_ID = 0x0000
OS doesn't load BT driver due to Sub_System_ID missmatch

solution: TOP-14807: Don't set AUX_HW_LOCK_2.

Summary: [MSFT][SURFACE][CO_VAL][PTL][McKenna][FmP] Event viewer - System error "Has determined that the network adapter is not functioning properly" observed while running S4 cycling -- 0x1000971
Custom field (Root Cause):
Bug root cause:
 - There are 2 active macs - BSS client and P2P client.
 - UMAC send 2 protection windows to LMAC - one for each mac.
 - LMAC start the first protection window.
 - Beacon is received, and LMAC remove the first protection window.
 - LMAC send NTF to UMAC that beacon is received.
 - LMAC allow PS.
 - PHY move to PS mode.
 - UMAC update 1 of the protection windows timing, and send it to LMAC.
   Since the current beacon event wasn't not removed yet, the UMAC send
   its window as well.
 - LMAC received hiscorical protection window, and set protection.
 - To configure the chain ant req, LMAC need to access the PHY.
   Since the PHY is in PS mode, we get assert when trying to access the PHY.

Fix:
If phy is not exist, coex status is off.
Check if coex status is not off before starting coex protection.

RC is the same as bug WIFI-527459. Fixed on: https://gerritwcs.ir.intel.com/c/wcd_fw-dev/+/177112

Custom field (Root Cause):
During execution, the mCtdpGetCurrentTemperatureApi stores provided callback arguments in CTDP context. Since this API relies on the FW response to get the current temperature from FW, this response may take time (as in this case - JS is busy). So when the next caller calls this API, it replaces the previously stored callback's arguments with its own. And that's what happened here. 
When the response started executing and working with the context, the memory that CTDP context is pointing to was already released by the next caller because of failure in sending FW command (transport layer was closed already). And this caused to the BSOD.

Summary: [HP][Quanta]-[Voco][MTL][Win11 22H2] [Assert 0x20003207]Wi-Fi list showed "No Wi-Fi networks found" when connected/disconnected miracast with BT LE headset connected.(Intel BE200)
Custom field (Root Cause):
[BUGFIX]  Coex: Fix Sync2Bt Timer Loss Sync

(-) Bug:
     Sync2Bt Timer is keep expired since in the past and prevent any LMAC other activity.

(-) Bug Description:
    Sync2BT Timer is use sync2BtRise-Timestamp in order to set the next timer expiration..
    But when the Sync2BtRise-Timestamp is in the past and not advanced for a long time
    it result with continues Sync2BtTimer expired and actually prevent any LMAC other activity

(-) Bug Scenario:
     Sync2Bt is enabled & working on timer, WiFi is on LB
     During that, WiFi is triggered Calbrations on HB which result with Phy LB Deactivate
     and Aux Phy Activate on HB. Following that on FullCoexOff we set Sync2BT Disable reason = SYNC_2_BT_BT_PROTOCOL_DIS
     Status: Sync2Bt is enabled from BT Side but since we are on HB now the Disable reason should allow all Tx but the tracking should continue.

    Then following mailbox we get to sync2BtEngineStatusUpdate() with sync2BT enabled status.
    but on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts() since we ask for sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed() we disable the sync2Bt kick filter
    while the Sync2Bt machnisem (timer) is stiil working.

Bug Solution :
  (-) Remove the dependency of sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts.
       Following that  as long as Sync2BT is enabled the Sync2BT mechanism will keep working even when we enter to HB Phy.
       Only in case Sync2BT is disabled (by BT MBX or by CI change) the Sync2BT mechanism will disabled.
       Note - When Sync2BT mechanism is working but Phy is on Non LB (Aux\Calib) the Tx will allowed and not defered.

  (-) Disable Sync2Bt Timer & Enable Resync by Sync2Bt by ISR.

Summary: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][MorganG][Intel RPL][Intel AX 211][WIFI][Win11]The call to the IntelIHVPipeClient interface failed, causing the computer cloning function to fail.
Custom field (Root Cause):
Since PC migration doesn't call FreeLibrary for MurocApi DLL, the destructor that suppose to close PIE and PipeClient threads is not called. It's an incorrect behavior by the PC migration.
Up until 22.220, PIE and PipeClient used CreateThread API to open those threads, threads that are created using this API are closed (not gracefully) when the process is closed.
In 22.230, CreateThread API was replaced with std::async API, threads that are created by std::async must be closed before closing the process, otherwise the process will keep running.
In order to mitigate such an incorrect behavior, we changed std::async back to CreateThread.

Summary: [HP][Win11][CFL][ThP2][Tobago][BSOD 0x124] System hang up with black screen and BSOD 0x124 occurred when running S3/S4 stress test
Custom field (Root Cause):
cc51: ca0d5c43533964b034e84aa44a9e9c037269729e
Not needed for any other core (yet), seen on ThP only.

Flush PCI pipe before completing the PNP_SET_POWER task.
Fix for a race that was found on weak CPU/PCI, where
driver is writing into a CSR, however, the actual right occurs
after we complete the PNP_SET_POWER task.
This causes WHEA unrecoverable error and leading to BSOD 0x124.
Due to weak CPU, or might be a combination with multiple
PCI bridges on this platform, the actual write is not instant.

For some reason, issue was not seen on Win10, while stated appearing
on Win11 - might be different PCI error handling logic.

Deeper analysis: it was seen using PCI analyzer that after driver
is completing the PNP_SET_POWER task, OS puts the PCI in low power mode,
and no further transactions are allowed. However, then we see a memory
write TLP - our CSR write, which was obviously initiated before.

As a WA, need to “flush” the PCI, by reading from the last written CSR
before competing the task. This should ensure that all previous
transactions have completed and it is safe to put PCI into sleep.

Summary: [HUAQIN][ASUS][AX211][RPL][22H2][22.200] System cannot connect to specific AP (But RTK, QC WLAN PASS)
Custom field (Root Cause):
The bug occurs with known misbehaving AP which advertises ECSA with CS-to-self
in its probe responses (not in beacons)
We saw this behavior in the past and implemented  DCR-261 (WREQ-36392) which allows us to connect to such APs
But in this setup the AP advertises operating class = 0x1a (26) while we’re in China MCC domain 0x434E (I see this in the RLG log didn’t find Country IE in AP beacons/probes)
According to the table E-6 in Annex E in the spec this operating class is invalid for China
So when we try to determine if the ECSA contains CS to self we attempt to retrieve the band by operating class + channel number, and since such operating class doesn’t exist
 in the current MCC we conclude that the CS is not CS to self, since the band is different (INVALID_BAND) though the channel number is the same
and thus we exclude such candidate and don’t connect though our competitors such as QCOM and RTEK do
The system requirement was to ignore the operating class in this specific case and assume the same band as the old one

Summary: [ASUS][RPL][GfP2][22.190]Wi-Fi will be not able to search 5Ghz AP SSID when using 2.4Ghz during WiDi screen casting
Custom field (Root Cause):
[BUGFIX] mvm: don't account for the losing time of the wrong link

    When we want to look for a hole for an event, and our event is placed
    after event B, we want to make sure that we leave room for the link that
    runs event B to loose the medium properly before we run our event.
    In case of GO / BSS in SCM, we can have the following scenario:

    GO's beacon saver ends at 100
    BSS'es TBTT ends at 50

    This means that we could place an event at 101 since the losing time of
    the GO is 0, but we don't since we want to leave enough time for the
    losing for the client.

    This wouldn't be a big problem if we didn't have to re-allocate events.
    I saw in USIM the following problem:

    1) time is now 50
    2) GO / BSS in SCM, beacon of the GO is at 150, beacon of the BSS at 100
    3) Fragmented scan allocates events (50 ms long)
    4) We place one time NOA for a fragment of the scan at time 180, after
       the next beacon of the GO (because of the beacon saver)
       Note that this overrides the BSS's TBTT which is fine.
    5) the beacon saver event of the GO ends at 180 to give room for the
       scan event
    6) time passes by, we are at 100
    7) TBTT of the BSS runs and we remove the occurrence after beacon Rx
    8) Refresh
    9) we place again the the scan's fragment, but this time we place it at
       180 + BSS's losing time.
    <=== This is the bug ===>

    We just moved the fragmented scan's event, but we had a NOA that was
    placed exactly for that specific event and now the fragmented scan's
    event is unfortunate because of the beacon saver of the GO.

    We could have placed the fragmented scan's event again at 180 because
    the client already knows it needs to have left the channel by 180. But
    because we take into account the losing time of the BSS after an event
    that belongs to the GO, we delay the scan event by 4ms and it misses the
    window created by the GO's NOA.

    Fix this by looking at the losing time of the link of the specific event
    that precedes the hole, and do not consider all the events in the
    binding.

Summary: [Huawei][Quanta][H99E][NobelF][AX201][21H2][WLAN] [AX201][805737181 ]After the WiFi driver is upgraded to version 160, there are more than 900 unknown threads in the message center, which are always blocked, and this problem occurs only after the driver i
Custom field (Root Cause):
Those threads are opened by a "KeepAlive" timer which runs a function every second to check if the connection to RPC is still valid.
The connection to RPC check is done by running an API that is sent to the RPC server, if the API fails, it returns an error.
When the Wlanext.exe process is in "pending" state, the RPC server doesn't respond to the RPC call which blocks the call forever (Bug in MSRPC).
Since the call is blocked, and the timer is still running, every second another thread is being stuck, and this is why there are so many threads.
To solve this, I put a boolean that signals if there is already a running thread, if there is already a running thread, the function will exit without doing anything.

Summary: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][MorganF][Intel ADL][Intel AX 211][WIFI][Win11]The PIE service has stuck cause to GetSupportedChannels does not return a value.
Custom field (Root Cause):
PIE is using an asynchronous method in order to send a bind event, in this case there was a racing condition between that method and the FreeLibrary call:
1) Asynchronous method is called.
2) Router frees the PIE IHV module while the method is still working.
3) The asynchronous method is still working while the main thread of the DLL that host that method is closed.
4) This causes Wlanext.exe process to remain open.
5) On driver enable, a new Wlanext.exe process is created.
6) Since there are 2 running Wlanext.exe processes, this means that the RPC server is still working in the old process which prevents creating a new RPC server connection in the new process.
7) PIE service tries to connect to the RPC server which is stuck on the old process, which makes the service to also be stuck.

Channel 149 is passive in EEPROM (not allowed for GO Activation)

Summary: [Xiaomi][ARL][HrP2/AX201][i5-11320H] LE Ext Adv scan result delay more than 20s+ sometime, very low performance compare with MTK chipset with BT24.10PV
Custom field (Root Cause):
Root cause:

We are switching to secondary channel only when primary offset is lesser than secondary offset. This is wrong, this will result in two problems,

When we received the primary packet at the beginning of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to secondary channel though secondary offset is still far. This makes bad utilization of remaining scan window and end up with fewer primary packet detection.
 When we received the primary packet at the end of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to primary channel though secondary offset is near. This makes secondary job to get into past and eventually we release the entry from scan data base. This will add delay for the detection for the secondary PDU.

Summary: [Surface][PTL+FmP2][24.0.1.1][PHY]Failing - RF/TRM/CA/BV-16-C [EDR Synchronization Sequence and Trailer]
Custom field (Root Cause):
The issue was in the function that handles the TX for the packet
header.
A race condition between the BMC pushing data towards BRI MP FIFO,
while the CSR write to TX modem TX FIFO (over BRI LP FIFO) did not
arrive to the CRF.
This causes, under specific timing conditions, cause the TX FIFO reset
to arrive to the CRF after the first MP BRI data (18 bit) arrive to
TX FIFO, leading to corrupt data seen over the other end.

Custom field (Root Cause):
WiAMT loads its WiFi FW very early (before BIOS runs),
WiFi FW runs FSEQ. As part of FSEQ it sets FINE locks (in particular AUX_HW_LOCK_2)
There is a logic in the top that prevent HW to write to registers when AUX_HW_LOCK_2 is set and relevant func_state is LOW
Relevant logic preventing BT OTP Reader (usee BT UMAC master) writing to Aux while BT func_state is LOW:
bt_umac_aux_connect_we_func_lock    = (~scu_aux_hw_lock_2 || bt_scu_func_state) && bt_umac_aux_connect_we;
When BIOS switches BT I/F to IOSF, BT HW kicks BT OTP Reader
OTP Reader tries writing to Aux register to enable OTP, but fails due to the early lock (BT func_state is LOW on this HW stage)
All next reads from OTP are failed since OTP is not enabled
BT config space remains with default values. In specific Sub_System_ID = 0x0000
OS doesn't load BT driver due to Sub_System_ID missmatch

Solution: AUX_HW_LOCK_2 (bit [8]) in SCU fine locks register (cnvi_scu_cnvi_scu_lock @0x6EAC).

Summary: [Xiaomi][RPL/ARL][AX211][i5-11320H] LE Ext Adv scan result delay more than 20s+ sometime, very low performance compare with MTK chipset.
Custom field (Root Cause):
Root cause:

We are switching to secondary channel only when primary offset is lesser than secondary offset. This is wrong, this will result in two problems,

When we received the primary packet at the beginning of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to secondary channel though secondary offset is still far. This makes bad utilization of remaining scan window and end up with fewer primary packet detection.
 When we received the primary packet at the end of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to primary channel though secondary offset is near. This makes secondary job to get into past and eventually we release the entry from scan data base. This will add delay for the detection for the secondary PDU.

when ext adv on primary channel is received during init

for D0 entry doorbell interrupt in some corner case scenario during
stress test. It is confirmed from the debugging that controller was

Summary: CLONE - [Lenovo ThinkPad JP][Thames2/LnL/FmP][QS][PCIe] BT Device lost due to TOP exception during S4 cycle - Clean WA from FW/Driver to retrieve debug
Custom field (Root Cause):
While executing a D3 scenario, prior to entering D0, we observed incorrect PCIE context info, which we suspect is due to an unidentified bug in the hardware. Consequently, the firmware (FW) triggered a fatal exception, leading to a soft reset of the CPU. During this soft reset, we encountered an additional Top exception rewriting all original exception data that was alraedy recorded in persistent.

The details of this Top exception suggest an issue that occurred during the initialization of the FSEQ following the soft reset due to original exception. However, the extra details provided by the Top exception data was inconclusive as per Top team. We assume that the hardware may have already been in a bad state due to the original issue when FW attempted to program the FSEQ as part of the initialization after the soft reset.

Due to the current exception handling approach, we lacked adequate data for debugging.

Proposed Solution: To address this issue, systems suggested halting the CPU immediately after any exception occurs. This will allow the host to collect debug information related to the exception before the firmware proceeds further and trigger further exceptions due to any instability already in the system.

Summary: [Samsung][Odin2-15/TGL/HrP2] Multi-Control (SPP) cannot connect to android tablet. (cherry pick fix of DUT sends LMP_Set_AFH as a peripheral)

sending LMP_Set_AFH following the role switch.

The root cause for this issue is a race between the processing of
RS message and lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet.

RS and LMP don't pass the same flow:
Role switch related messages:	BC-> LC-> LLC-> LM
PDU packet reception:		BC-> LC-> LM

Since PDU packet reception has fewer steps than RS, LM may move to the
new role (slave role) too late.
When lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet is received at LM,
LM layer can still be in the old role (master)
i.e., LM is in old role, and LC is in the new role.

As a fix, the setup complete process is postponed till RS message is
processed by LM layer.

During Encryption setup procedure, in some cases multiple retransmission of LMP_Accepted, LMP_Key_Size_req was happening after the LMP_start_encryption request is initiated by Master. Which was causing the payload counter mismatch between Master and Slave.
Solution: Before transmitting lmp-start-enc-pdu, ensure that our ack for the
previous packet ( lmp accepted for key size ) is received. We can
confirm this when the remote device sends a NULL packet.

Summary: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][Morgan][Intel TGL][Intel AX 201][BT][Win11]The DUT connect fail with phone during running stress test(FW Fatal exception and Hardware error observed)
Custom field (Root Cause):
During pairing process, while calculating the DHkey, locally generated
key handle for that particular BR/EDR link to be fetched and validated.
To fetch the keyhandle( pertaining to the link), we pass link index, and this
index was wrong, resulting in fetching a wrong key handle for that link.

Wrong index is fetched, because the Array(au8SSPDHKeyRequestedId) holding
the identifiers has duplicate entries. But this array is expected to have unique identifiers
for each and every BR/EDR link.

Why Array has duplicate entries, because array is updated with identifiers
by incrementing a static variable( u8NextSSPDHKeyCalcId),in multiples of 2.
And this variable is unsigned integer which can hold a maximum of value 255.
And in case of multiple pair-unpair operations, this variable will wrap around.
So we may end up with duplicate entries in the array.

Summary: [Samsung][TGL/CFL/JfP/HrP/TyP][Win10/Win11] BT mouse/keyboard does not work if trying to use it after leaving it about 10+ minutes or turn it off and on
Custom field (Root Cause):
LT_ADDR mismatch is the cause for the paging procedure to fail.

When we get page req from any device & post baseband connection if we don't succeed, on newconnection timeout we are not clearing the LT_ADDR stored against the same linkIndex.

On the subsequent paging on any LT_ADDR different from the previous failing LT_ADDR will result in mismatch because it has the old LT_ADDR retained & the because of design we OR the LT_ADDR in a link.

we clear the LT_ADDR in a linkindex only when we start the pagescan not in the subsequent resume pagescan post failed to establish a connection as seen above.

Summary: [Samsung][Venus-13/TGL/TyP2][SmartThings][20H2] Lost address information of connectable adv from non-connectable advertising during ModernStandby
Custom field (Root Cause):
Windows BT stack does not use LL Privacy yet. Hence, it is responsible for periodic refreshing of the random address of ADV instances it owns. The period is assumed to be 15 mins with a margin of +-1min. The address refresh works fine when the PC is in S0. But, when the PC is in Modern Connected Standby, Windows BT stack stops refreshing the random address due to a bug. This causes Privacy issue (device is trackable as the MAC address remains same for as long as the device is in Modern Standby) as well as a breakdown in SmartThings functionality.
Controller resets the GATT Instance Addr field in Offload ADV instance Service Data if the address has not been refreshed for an hour. The address in this field is used by the remote device to identify the connectable ADV coming from the same device. Even though a connectible ADV is present, due to the field being set to 0, the remote device cannot connect to the device causing SmartThings functionality to breakdown.
Privacy issue in Windows platforms can only be fixed by MSFT. So, that is out of scope of this jira ticket. The fix here is to make sure that SmartThings functionality will still work with the accepted loss of privacy.
The fix done is to not reset the GATT instance MAC address field on PID rotation 1 hr timer expiry while GATT ADV instance is still enabled for advertising.
